hints: Look past the different formulas and focus on what type of reaction is happening in both cases.

Write the ionic equation for reaction 1, strong acid plus strong base gives $\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{OH}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$, and count how many moles of water are made.
Since reaction 2 makes the same number of moles of water from strong acid and strong base, compare its total heat released to reaction 1.
walkthrough:
**Recognise Both as Neutralisation**

Both reactions mix a strong acid with a strong base to make salt plus water. That means the real chemical change is the same in both.

$$\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{OH}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$$

**Count the Moles of Water**

In reaction 1, $2\text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ makes $2$ moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. In reaction 2, $\text{Ba}(\text{OH})_2 + 2\text{HCl}$ also makes $2$ moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$$\text{moles of H}_2\text{O} = 2 \text{ in both reactions}$$

**Apply the Same Enthalpy**

Spectator ions like $\text{Na}^+$, $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ stay in solution and release almost no heat. So the enthalpy depends only on forming water, about $-57$ kJ per mole of water.

$$2 \times (-57) = -114 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Conclude the Answer**

Because both equations form the same amount of water from strong acid and strong base, their enthalpy changes will be essentially identical, so reaction 2 is also about $-114$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.

options.A: Incorrect. $-57$ kJ mol-1 is the enthalpy for forming only 1 mole of water. Both reactions form 2 moles of water, so you should not halve the $-114$ value.
options.B: Incorrect. There is no chemical reason to get $-76$ kJ mol-1 here. It is a distractor value with no link to the $\text{H}^+ + \text{OH}^-$ neutralisation.
options.C: Correct. Both are strong acid plus strong base neutralisations forming 2 moles of water, so the ionic equation and heat released are the same, giving $-114$ kJ mol-1.
options.D: Incorrect. $-228$ kJ mol-1 comes from doubling $-114$ by mistake. Do not double again, both equations already include 2 moles of water.
